title: Electron Ptychography Resolves Individual Atomic Layers in Twisted Super-Moiré
content: Twisted moiré systems have attracted considerable attention due to their tunable electronic and optical properties enabled by interlayer coupling modulated by the twist angle, leading to emergent phenomena such as superconductivity, correlated insulating states, and unconventional ferroelectricity [1]. While most studies have focused on small-angle twisted systems, a new supermoiré lattice has been identified near large commensurate twist angles, exhibiting robust periodicity and flat-band engineerability [2]. Unlike conventional moiré lattices formed by simple AA or AB stacking patterns at small twist angles, the supermoiré domains arise from more complex commensurate stacking arrangements, referred to as commensurate rotational faults (CRFs) [3], making their characterization particularly challenging. In this work, we employ multislice electron ptychography [4] to clearly resolve the individual layer structures of bilayer–bilayer twisted WSe2 near the 21.8° commensurate angle, successfully identifying three distinct CRF structures that collectively form the supermoiré lattice.
